entries.title: V01 close-out: N02 production deployment ACTUALLY fixed + build-provenance footer + V01 ✅
entries.body:
V01 — the v2 transparency platform skeleton — formally closes ✅ this session, but
the close-out audit surfaced two substantive issues that this entry both documents
and fixes. The plan row flips `🟡 2026-05-12 → ✅ 2026-05-19`.

### What this session shipped

1. **N02 production deployment ACTUALLY fixed.** The portal's
   `platform/data/governance.json` showed N02 as `available: False, n_artifacts: 0,
   synthesis_md: ""` for the entire window between PR #2 merging at 2026-05-19 18:18
   UTC and this session — despite the prior `9.0.8+build-2026-05-19.1` entry claiming
   N02 was "live in production". See the **inline correction below** on the
   `9.0.8+build-2026-05-19.1` entry for the root-cause analysis. This session copied
   the missing N02 outputs from the parent repo into the worktree, regenerated
   `platform/data/*.json` (governance.json now 67 KB with N02 actually populated:
   61 artifacts, 20K-char synthesis, 61 summaries, the v2 audit's 1,477 findings
   surfaced), and committed them to engine git so future publishes from any worktree
   find them.

2. **Build-provenance footer (user-visible).** The portal footer now renders a
   compact monospace row beneath the existing "Generated" line:
   ```text
   engine 33d0048 on claude/mystifying-curie-ce5953
     · N01 critic-2026-05-11 (1,999 findings · $256)
     · N02 bias-audit-2026-05-12 (cfg 1401d8ce · corpus a5adf5ca · $45)
   ```
   This makes the transparency claim structurally self-disclosing — every page on the
   portal shows which engine commit produced its data and which governance audits
   scored the corpus. The rendering is conditional (`{buildStateData.engine_commit_short
   && ...}`) so older portal builds without the new fields keep building cleanly.

3. **`platform/src/` sync-gap finding documented (deferred to V02).** Discovered
   during the audit: `scripts/publish_progress.sh` only syncs `platform/data/` from
   engine to portal, not the rest of `platform/`. Several files exist portal-only
   (`platform/src/lib/data.ts`, `lib/utils.ts`, `app/scenarios/page.tsx`,
   `app/sample-briefs/page.tsx`, `public/sample-briefs/*.pdf` × 8, `package-lock.json`).
   Root cause: engine `.gitignore` line 34 (`lib/`, intended for Python build
   artifacts) catches `platform/src/lib/` too. Fix requires non-trivial scope
   expansion; deferred to V02 (which already touches the deployment pipeline).
   Documented in detail in `implementation/steps/V01_platform_v2_skeleton/HANDOFF.md`.

### New

- **`implementation/steps/V01_platform_v2_skeleton/NOTES.md`** — session log with
  full timeline of V01 across all sessions + this session's discoveries.
- **`implementation/steps/V01_platform_v2_skeleton/DELTA.md`** — consolidated file
  inventory across all V01 sessions.
- **`implementation/steps/V01_platform_v2_skeleton/HANDOFF.md`** — close-out brief
  + open follow-ups in priority order.
- **`implementation/steps/V01_platform_v2_skeleton/OUTPUT/MANIFEST.md`** — pointer
  to in-place artifacts (V01's outputs are full deployed infra; OUTPUT/ doesn't
  archive them — matches N02 convention).
- **N02 run outputs committed to engine git** for the first time:
  `runs/bias-audit-2026-05-12/manifest.json`, `synthesis.md`, `n01_n02_crossref.md`,
  and `per_artifact/*.json` × 61. ~13 MB total. Previously lived only in the parent
  repo's local working tree.
- **Portal PR #4** opens this session — adds the footer rendering + extends
  `BuildStateData` interface with optional provenance fields. URL:
  https://github.com/milad9595naeimi/GIPRE-Transparency/pull/4

### Changed

- **`scripts/build_site_data.py`** — added `import subprocess`, `_git_head_info()`
  helper (engine git HEAD: full + short SHA, ISO commit time, branch name),
  `_read_run_manifest()` helper (safe JSON load for run manifest.json files), and
  extended `parse_build_state()` to merge in N01 + N02 manifest provenance fields
  (run_id, started_utc, n_corpus_artifacts, n_judges, total_usd, config_hash,
  corpus_hash, total_findings). All fields land in `platform/data/build_state.json`
  and are consumed by the portal footer.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** — added inline correction to `9.0.8+build-2026-05-19.1` per
  below.
- **`implementation/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`** — V01 row status flipped
  `🟡 2026-05-12` → `✅ 2026-05-19`.
- **Closed stale portal PR #3** (would have re-deployed empty N02 governance.json
  if merged). Replacement auto-publish PR from this session's engine HEAD carries
  the populated data.

### Architecture moves

- **First multi-PR portal coordination.** Until this session every portal change
  rode the single auto-publish lane via `scripts/publish_progress.sh`. This session
  proved the pattern for portal-side source changes (PR #4) coordinating with the
  auto-publish data PR — necessary until the `platform/src/` sync gap is closed.

entries.title: N02 shipped to production + continuous-publish infrastructure
entries.body:
> ⚠️ **CORRECTION 2026-05-19 (V01 close-out)**: the "N02 live at production URL" claim
> in this entry is incorrect. Verification at V01 close-out showed
> `portal/main:platform/data/governance.json` had N02 as `available: False,
> n_artifacts: 0, synthesis_md: ""` after PR #2 merged — the merge diff stat
> `governance.json | 560 +----------` meant PR #2 **deleted** the N02 block rather
> than publishing it. Root cause: `scripts/publish_progress.sh` ran
> `build_site_data.py` from a worktree that was missing N02's `synthesis.md`,
> `per_artifact/*.json`, and `manifest.json` (those files lived only in the parent
> repo's working tree, never `git add`'d). The generator emitted an empty `n02`
> block; PR #2 published the empty version. The "Mark N02 as live" engine commit
> `33d0048` and the auto-publish portal PR #3 that followed both perpetuated the
> incorrect state. **N02 was actually deployed to production in the V01 close-out
> session (entry `9.0.9+build-2026-05-19.2` above).**

Following the N02 Bias Auditor build below, two production-readiness events landed:

**N02 live at production URL.** Portal PR #2 (auto-published from engine commit `4c7de21`) merged
to portal `main` at 18:18 UTC; Azure SWA production redeploy succeeded; the deployed site at
https://ashy-forest-072686a0f.7.azurestaticapps.net now shows the v2 audit's 1,477 findings on
the Governance page (replacing the 2026-05-13 1,057-finding snapshot). PR #2:
https://github.com/milad9595naeimi/GIPRE-Transparency/pull/2 (merged). [^correction]

[^correction]: ⚠️ This sentence is incorrect — see correction at the top of this entry.
PR #2's merge diff stat was `governance.json | 560 +---------- (deletions)`; it emptied
N02 rather than publishing it. N02 was actually deployed in the V01 close-out session
on 2026-05-19. Left in place to preserve the historical state of what was believed at
the time the entry was written.

**Continuous-publish infrastructure landed.** `scripts/publish_progress.sh` is now the canonical
one-shot publisher — call after every meaningful unit of work to rebuild platform data, commit,
push engine (private `origin`), open auto-publish PR on portal (public), and verify Azure deploy.
Hard safety check at step [0/6] aborts if `origin` doesn't point to the engine private repo (this
safety exists because the first version leaked engine code to the public portal before the check
was added). Codified as mandatory in SESSION_START_TEMPLATE rule 9, SESSION_END_TEMPLATE §1 step 3
items 8-12, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN §6, and the `feedback_session_end_checklist.md` memory rule.

**Two-repo design**:
- `origin` = private engine repo `milad9595naeimi/Geopolitical_Model_AI_Agents` — full IP
- `portal` = public portal repo `milad9595naeimi/GIPRE-Transparency` — Azure SWA deploy target

**Production URL** (what prospective clients see): https://ashy-forest-072686a0f.7.azurestaticapps.net

entries.title: Second governance pass: L50 + L65 Bias Auditor (Step N02)
entries.body:
The L50 (Critical Bias Auditor) + L65 (Cultural Bias Auditor) **Bias Auditor** ran in faithful
mode against the same 61-artifact v4 corpus N01 audited. Methodology: Doc 1 §2.50 + §T.3.10,
implementing BorderLines NAACL 2024 (disputed-territory cross-language stance probes), Tao
PNAS Nexus 2024 (cultural-prompting delta), Identity-Aware arXiv 2510.18510 (6 behavioural
criteria as scorecard dims), Khandelwal EMNLP 2025 (open-ended > MCQ for cultural alignment),
and Acharya multiplex 4-feature checklist as structural rubric.

**Audit verdict: 2 / 61 publish_ok, 30 / 61 revise, 29 / 61 needs_substantive_revision** —
the Bias Auditor surfaced **1,477 findings** across the 61 artifacts (mean 24.2 per artifact),
composite-score distribution mean **57.3 / 100** (range 39.2 – 75.5). Bottom decile dominated
by regional/master synthesis + v4 PDF artifacts where structural lens-panel-diversity is
degenerate at aggregation level; LLM-rated dims (Eurocentric framing + 6 Identity-Aware)
scored 37-48 / 100 for these.

**N01 ↔ N02 convergence**: cross-reference at `runs/bias-audit-2026-05-12/n01_n02_crossref.md`
shows **422 of N01's 813 bias-relevant findings independently confirmed by N02** (52%
substring-overlap-matched), with **599 additional N02-only findings** in categories N01 doesn't
audit (source-region-imbalance, cohort-fairness-gap, cross-language-divergence,
intra-cultural-blindness). The independent convergence validates the multi-pass governance
design.

### New
- **`gipre/governance/bias_auditor/` package** (~2,500 LoC across 5 files) was scaffolded in
  the prior step but completed + run end-to-end this session:
  - `runner.py` (1,505 LoC) — corpus loader, multi-vendor jury dispatch, multi-round debate,
    probe-pass orchestrator with resume-from-checkpoint streaming-write, aggregation merging
    structural + probe + LLM-rated dims into 13-dim composite, output writers.
  - `schema.py` (309 LoC) — 13-dim rubric (Eurocentric + 6× Identity-Aware + 4 structural + 2
    probe), 8 finding categories, validators.
  - `structural_metrics.py` (410 LoC) — Python-only deterministic metrics: Shannon-entropy
    lens-panel diversity (declared + TF-actual), URL-domain region classifier, actor-catalogue
    regional balance via KL-divergence vs. world-pop+GDP.
  - `probes.py` (212 LoC) — 30 active probes (10 BorderLines + 10 Identity-Aware + 10
    Khandelwal) × 5 language-personas (en/zh/ar/fa/es) with grounded system prompts.
  - `__init__.py` — package init.
- **`config/bias_auditor.yaml`** — locked v2 jury composition: 3 DeepSeek-V4-Pro + 2 Claude
  Sonnet 4.6 + 2 GPT-4o; cap_usd $200; 13-dim rubric weights summing to 100; 30 active probes
  × 5 language-personas; DeepSeek vendor concurrency=2.
- **`agents/governance/bias_auditor.md`** (~210 lines) — production spec.
- **`tests/test_bias_auditor_smoke.py`** (16 tests, all green) — schema validation, rubric
  weights-sum check, config load, probe registry shape, structural-metrics unit tests,
  URL-domain classifier, KL-divergence math, dry-run, cost forecast.
- **`scripts/run_bias_audit.py`** — CLI launcher.
- **`scripts/crossref_n01_n02.py`** — N01 ↔ N02 convergence analyser (category-mapping +
  substring overlap heuristic).
- **`scripts/mirror_run_to_parent.sh`** (new this session) — continuous mirror of audit run
  state from worktree to parent repo + timestamped snapshot retention.
- **`implementation/steps/N02_bias_auditor_run/RECOVERY.md`** (new this session) — recovery
  procedure documentation covering every failure mode (process kill, Claude Code crash,
  worktree deletion, machine reboot, vendor outage, aggregation bug).
- **Run output at `runs/bias-audit-2026-05-12/`**:
  - `synthesis.md` (26 KB) — human-readable aggregate report with gate distribution + bottom
    decile + top-10 per category + per-persona probe breakdown.
  - `per_artifact/<id>.json` × 61 — per-artifact 13-dim composite + raw judge verdicts.
  - `structural_metrics.csv` (62 rows) — Python-computed structural numbers.
  - `probe_results.csv` — cross-language probe responses.
  - `manifest.json` — run provenance (config_hash 1401d8cea7263072, corpus_hash
    a5adf5cae682aa8f, 7 judges, $44.91 spend, 1,654 calls).
  - `n01_n02_crossref.md` — convergence analysis.

### Changed
- **`gipre/llm/deepseek_client.py`** — added `PER_CALL_TIMEOUT_S = 90.0` (env-var overridable)

entries.title: First governance pass: L54 Critic / Multi-Model Jury (Step N01)
entries.body:
The L54 Critic ran in faithful mode (per Doc 1 §2.54 + CALM Ye et al. ICLR 2025 + adaptive Beta-Binomial
stability arXiv 2510.12697) against the complete v4 corpus: 61 artifacts (30 actors + 10 themes + 5 lenses
+ 8 syntheses + 8 PDFs). The 7-judge jury combined 3 vendors — Anthropic (Opus 4.7 generalist + Sonnet 4.6
regional-studies-expert + Haiku 4.5 bandwagon-detector), OpenAI (GPT-5 skeptical-quant + GPT-4o
calibration-auditor), and DeepSeek V4-Pro (Tianxia non-Western framing + devil's-advocate). Each artifact
ran 4-5 rounds of multi-round debate with judges seeing other judges' findings (scores hidden to
suppress bandwagon bias) and KS-stability early-stopping. A CALM-12 perturbation pass on 6 stratified-sample
artifacts produced per-judge bias profiles across the 5 critical biases for single-artifact scoring mode
(verbosity, self-enhancement, authority, diversity, style).

**Audit verdict: 0/61 publish_ok, 61/61 revise, 0/61 needs_human_review.** The Critic uniformly judged
the existing v4 corpus as requiring revision before publication, surfacing **1,999 findings** across the
61 artifacts (mean 32.8 per artifact; ~150 critical-severity). Score distribution tight: mean 56.1, stdev
3.7, range 43.8-63.0. The audit validated the methodological choice to run N01 before B03-B06 (300+ more
agents): catching systematic schema bugs, lens-balance failures, and arithmetic inconsistencies BEFORE
scaling.

### New
- **`gipre/governance/` package** (~1,030 LoC across 5 files):
  - `critic.py` (620 LoC) — main runner: corpus loader (JSON + pypdf-extracted PDF text), 7-judge multi-vendor
    dispatch via `ThreadPoolExecutor`, multi-round debate state machine, artifact-level parallelism
    (`max_parallel_artifacts=3`), bootstrap 95% CI aggregation, cost-cap enforcement, output writers.
  - `critic_schema.py` (220 LoC) — extended `GOVERNANCE_CRITIC_OUTPUT_SCHEMA` with `QualityScores`,
    `CALMBiasScores`, `Finding`, `JudgeVerdict`, `AggregateJuryVerdict` dataclasses; client-side validators.
  - `em_beta_binomial.py` (165 LoC) — EM solver for time-varying Beta-Binomial mixture per arXiv
    2510.12697, KS-distance helper, `StabilityState` tracker, `should_stop_debate` entry point.
  - `calm_perturbations.py` (140 LoC) — 5 critical CALM-12 perturbations (verbosity, self-enhancement,
    authority, diversity, style) with deterministic seeding + RR/CR computation.
  - `__init__.py` — package init.
- **`gipre/llm/openai_client.py`** (175 LoC) — direct OpenAI API shim mirroring `deepseek_client.py`.
  Handles GPT-5 / o-series `max_completion_tokens` rename + dropped-temperature-parameter. `dispatch_judge()`
  helper. Cost log at `runs/_openai_costs.jsonl`.
- **`gipre/llm/anthropic_client.py`** (155 LoC) — direct Anthropic Messages API shim. Pre-emptively skips
  the deprecated `temperature` parameter on Opus 4.7+ models. `dispatch_judge()` helper. Cost log at
  `runs/_anthropic_costs.jsonl`.
- **`config/critic.yaml`** — 7-judge jury composition (3 Anthropic tiers + 2 OpenAI tiers + 2 DeepSeek
  personas), 7-dim rubric weights (clarity / accuracy / decision-relevance / balance / depth / persona-fit
  / actionability), CALM-12 bias-mitigation flags, KS-stability threshold (δ=0.05), max-rounds (5),
  perturbation stratification (sample of 6 across artifact classes), aggregation thresholds (pass-gate=70,
  high-disagreement-stddev=15), cost cap ($400), corpus globs, artifact-level parallelism (max=3).
- **`tests/test_critic_smoke.py`** — 18 smoke tests (schema validation, EM convergence on synthetic
  Beta-Binomial mixture, KS distance, stability state, perturbation determinism, RR/CR computation,
  forecast machinery, stratified sampling, dry-run, cost-cap abort path, verdict coercion, PDF extraction).
  **All 18 green.**
- **Run output** at `runs/critic-2026-05-11/`:
  - `synthesis.md` (353 KB) — human-readable aggregate report.
  - `critiques/<id>.json` × 61 — per-artifact full critique JSONs.
  - `bias_audit.csv` — 294 rows (per-judge × per-artifact × per-perturbation RR/CR).
  - `manifest.json` — run provenance (config hash, corpus hash, judges, costs).
- **OpenAI API key** added to `API Keys.docx` (user-provided, post-B01 `parse_api_keys()` machinery
  auto-picks up).
- **`agents/governance/critic.md`** — expanded from 30-line stub to ~200-line production spec
  (persona-specific guidance for all 7 judges, hard schema rules, critical-finding rule, anti-instructions,
  downstream integration mapping L20/L23/L36/L29).

### Changed
- **`implementation/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`**: N01 row status `⏳` → `🟡 2026-05-11` → `✅ 2026-05-12`
  (the second flip on user acceptance).

### Architecture moves
- **First non-MVC governance step shipped.** N01 wires the first faithful L54 implementation in the
  project. The 7-judge × 3-vendor jury is the first time the project has actually exercised multi-vendor
  heterogeneity at runtime — B01 wired DeepSeek for L17 only; N01 dispatches across Anthropic + OpenAI +
  DeepSeek simultaneously

entries.title: Theme half-coverage milestone: 10 → 40 active themes (Step B02)
entries.body:
The 30 new themes activated by B02 take the theme catalogue from 12.5% to 50% coverage of the
Doc 2 §3.1 v9.0 taxonomy. Each new theme carries a research-augmented spec (Contemporary signal
2025-2026 + Recent testable predictions + Hits and misses), a 6-10 source curated OSINT
allowlist, and per-category backbone routing per the B02 D4 rule: macro_financial ∪ technology_ai
∪ cross_cutting → claude-opus-4-7; rest → claude-sonnet-4-6. The L31 Theme Cascade layer
(`p(y_T|Sᵢ) = ∫ a(y)·∏_C∈T p(y_C|Sᵢ)·c_copula(Sᵢ) dy`, Doc 1 §2.4) now has 4× the input density
it had at end-B01 — directly unblocking richer theme briefs in the next PDF cycle.

### New
- **30 new theme spec files** in `agents/themes/`: T11 pandemic_biosecurity, T12 cyber_critical_infra, T13 election_integrity, T14 demographic_cliff, T15 religious_political, T16 quantum_geopolitics, T17 surveillance_tech, T18 pharma_api_supply, T19 antimicrobial_resistance, T20 civil_society_repression, T21 korean_peninsula, T22 sahel_instability, T23 ukraine_russia_europe, T24 latam_political_cycle, T25 dollar_funding_stress, T26 cb_divergence_currency, T27 commodity_cycles_inflation, T28 credit_cycles_nbfi, T29 shipping_chokepoints, T30 port_logistics_resilience, T31 water_stress_transboundary, T32 agricultural_shocks, T33 energy_transition_geopolitics, T34 judicial_independence, T35 mass_migration_refugee, T36 urbanisation_megacity, T37 gender_rights_regression, T38 criminal_economy_illicit_finance, T39 information_warfare, T40 space_geopolitics. Each spec carries indicators (6 with one fan-chart marked), lens priors (3-5 picks), seminal references (4-6), Contemporary signal (2025-2026) paragraph with real outlets + URLs + dates, 3-5 Recent testable predictions with predictor names, Hits and misses, and 3-5 cross-theme couplings with sign+strength+rationale.
- **`config/theme_sources.yaml`** — new file, parallel to `config/lens_sources.yaml` from B01. Curated authoritative-source allowlist of 6-10 sources per new theme (T11-T40), with `org / type / role / desc` fields. Backfill of T01-T10 deferred to a B02 follow-up.
- **`inactive_themes` tail extension** in `config/themes.yaml`: T41-T80 catalogued as id+name+category stubs across all 9 Doc 2 §3.1 categories, ready for activation in future steps without ID-collision risk.

- **`config/agents.yaml`**: roster_summary `total` 65 → 95, `themes` 10 → 40. 30 new theme rows appended. **Backbone flips per D4 per-category rule: T02, T06, T07 changed from `claude-sonnet-4-6` → `claude-opus-4-7`** (joins T10 already on opus). All new macro_financial / technology_ai / cross_cutting themes also on opus.

- **`AGENT_COVERAGE.md`** §1.2: theme-coverage table rewritten — 40 of 80 active, per-category balance, backbone per theme.
- **`EXPANSION_GUIDE.md`** Stage table and §2 Stage 1 scope: B02 marked ✅; agent count column updated; Stage 0.5 row added (95 agents).
- **`implementation/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`**: B02 status flipped 🟡 in-progress (→ ✅ at session-end acceptance).

### Architecture moves
- **Half-coverage milestone for the 80-theme catalogue.** L31 Theme Cascade now has 40 production-quality input agents instead of 10. Category balance hits the proportional-to-Doc-2-weights target (the B02 D1-B decision): each category sits at 40-57% activation, none in single digits.
- **Per-category backbone routing established as a convention.** D4 institutes the rule: macro_financial ∪ technology_ai ∪ cross_cutting agents on claude-opus-4-7 (where deep reasoning pays off); rest on claude-sonnet-4-6 (cost baseline). Mirrors the lens-panel pattern of per-school backbone choice from B01.

The `gipre.data.lens_grounding` machinery (B01) is designed to be reused for themes at brief-render time — the only extension needed is a `fetch_for_theme(theme_id)` helper, deferred to B02-followup.

entries.title: Lens panel completion + DeepSeek for L17 + per-lens OSINT grounding (Step B01)
entries.body:
The 20-lens panel declared in `config/lenses.yaml` is now fully active (50 → 65 agents). The Tianxia lens (L17) is the first agent in the project to route through a non-Anthropic vendor — DeepSeek V4-Pro — making good on the multi-vendor pluralism contract from Doc 6 Gap 6. Each lens now also pulls 1-2 fresh URLs from a curated authoritative-source allowlist at brief-time, so reasoning is grounded in current evidence rather than only seminal works.

### New
- **15 lens spec files** under `agents/lenses/`: L02 Wendt, L03 Ikenberry, L04 Krasner, L06 Reinhart-Rogoff, L07 Eichengreen, L08 Diamond-Dybvig, L09 Acemoglu-Robinson, L10 Linz-Stepan/Levitsky-Way, L11 Krugman, L12 Hubbert-Hotelling, L13 Romer, L14 Wyplosz, L15 Henderson, L16 Huntington (contested), L20 Neo-Ottoman. Each spec carries a "Contemporary signal (2025-2026)" + "Recent testable predictions" + "Recent hits and misses" section grounded in deep research (commentators, outlets, URLs, dates).
- **`gipre/llm/`** — new package. `gipre/llm/__init__.py` parses `API Keys.docx` for vendor keys (regex tolerant to the loose layout). `gipre/llm/deepseek_client.py` is the single-`chat()`-entry-point shim with retry, USD cost log to `runs/_deepseek_costs.jsonl`, and a `dispatch_lens()` helper that the orchestrator calls when `AgentRequest.backbone_route == "deepseek"`.
- **`gipre/data/lens_grounding.py`** — per-lens live OSINT grounding shim. `fetch_for(lens_id)` pulls 1-3 URLs from the lens's allowlist via `gipre.data.fetch.fetch` (parallel ThreadPoolExecutor, 5s timeout, browser User-Agent, 24h cache). `format_for_prompt()` renders snippets as a markdown block to inject into the lens user-prompt.
- **`config/lens_sources.yaml`** — curated authoritative allowlist of 8-12 sources per lens (all 20 lenses covered). L20 Neo-Ottoman is non-Western-weighted (6/10 non-Western: SETA, Insight Turkey, ORSAM, Daily Sabah, Tasnim, Middle East Eye). L16 Huntington explicitly mixes proponent / critic / data sources and tags each with a `stance` field.
- **Smoke tests**: `tests/test_deepseek_smoke.py` (3 tests, real DeepSeek API calls mandatory) + `tests/test_lens_grounding_smoke.py` (3 tests, real HTTP fetch for L13). 6/6 pass. Aggregate DeepSeek cost across smoke runs: ~$0.003.

### Changed
- **`config/agents.yaml`**: 15 new lens entries added; `roster_summary.total` 50 → 65, `roster_summary.lenses` 5 → 20. **L17 backbone changed from `claude-sonnet-4-6` to `deepseek-v4-pro`** with `route: deepseek` field added.

The orchestrator branches on `req.backbone_route` — empty string means Agent tool (default for the other 64 agents); `"deepseek"` means call the shim, which returns a JSON payload conforming to `LENS_OUTPUT_SCHEMA`.

The orchestrator pre-fetches before dispatch and injects the snippets into the lens user-prompt. Doc 1 §2.4 L52 date-aware retrieval is honoured (24h cache key via `date_floor=YYYY-MM-DD`).

entries.title: Multi-session framework scaffolding (Step S00)
entries.body:
The previous four iterations (v1→v4) cycled through the same first slice of the model.
This release stops that loop and installs the operating system that will drive the
remaining ~110 sessions of the v9.0 build.

### New
- **`implementation/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`** — master plan with 14 phases (A through N),
  ~110 sessions enumerated, status legend, and a next-three-session recommendation.
- **`implementation/SESSION_START_TEMPLATE.md`** — pasted into a new Claude Code session
  to begin a step. Encodes: read-first protocol, scope-confirmation gate, deep-research

  touching files outside the step folder, default acceptance-criteria checklist,

- **`implementation/steps/`** + **`implementation/completed_steps/`** directories.
- **Top-level `README.md`** — added "Multi-session build" pointer block.

### Step-folder convention (now standard for all future steps)
```
implementation/{steps|completed_steps}/<step_id>_<short_name>/
├── STEP.md      ← step definition (goal, scope, deliverables, acceptance criteria)
├── NOTES.md     ← research log + decisions made during session
├── OUTPUT/      ← artifacts produced
├── DELTA.md     ← list of files changed in broader project, with rationale

```

### Output / location
- `implementation/completed_steps/S00_framework_scaffolding/` (4 files: STEP, NOTES, DELTA, HANDOFF).

### Suggested next step
**B01 — Lens panel expansion** (50 → 61 agents). See HANDOFF.md in the S00 step folder for the full rationale.

### Carry-forward notes

entries.title: v4 narrative-integrated deep-analysis redesign
entries.body:
v3 had quantified impact and 12 maps but the user feedback caught three real issues:
(1) maps were dumped in a "Strategic Atlas" section instead of integrated with the
arguments that cite them; (2) the analysis was still summary-level rather than truly
deep (causal chains, historical analogues, counter-narratives missing); (3) tail risks
(less likely but high-impact "black swans") had no dedicated treatment. v4 fixes all
three plus tightens the palette and the page-overflow discipline.

### New
- **3 deep-research reports**:
  - `_research/v4_narrative_integration.md` — MGI/FT/Economist/BoE/RAND chart-in-narrative
    proximity rule; dual-tier captions; annotation-layer doctrine; Bridgewater composite
    index pattern; BoE conditioning-box discipline.
  - `_research/v4_tail_risks.md` — Eurasia Red Herrings + Atlantic Council Snow Leopards
    + GARP Inconceivable + Kahneman/Klein pre-mortem + CSIS Surprise-Is-Inevitable +
    Taleb antifragility. 12 tail-risk directives.
  - `_research/v4_probabilistic_forecasts.md` — BoE two-piece normal density + Fed
    disagreement-as-uncertainty + Bank of Canada 2025 pivot + NHC ellipses + Cascade
    Institute three coupling mechanisms + ICD 203 + Brier-score discipline.
- **`styles_v4.py`** — tighter palette (deep navy `#0F2A4A` primary, deep red `#A8001E`
  signal, restrained gold `#9C7A3A`, pure-white surface, less salmon than v3). 174mm
  safe-width discipline.
- **`charts_v4.py`** — new chart types: `causal_chain_diagram`, `cross_impact_matrix`,
  `bayesian_update_chart`, `historical_analogue_overlay`, `tail_risk_panel`,
  `quantified_impact_bar` (per-risk inline). v4 palette.
- **`pdf_builder_v4.py`** — narrative-integrated layout with new components:
  `DeepRiskSection` (per-risk dedicated 2-3pp narrative block), `TailRiskCard`,
  `CalloutBox` (v4 palette), no empty section dividers.
- **`region_brief_v4.py`** — full v4 orchestrator with 19-section structure:
  Cover → BLUF → Executive Summary + persona callouts → Top 10 Risks (each with
  dedicated multi-page block: lead, causal chain, second-order effects, historical
  analogue, counter-narrative, quantified impact, watch signals, business trigger,
  lens reading) → Tail Risks (Snow Leopards) → Master Scenarios + cross-impact →
  Bayesian Updates → Actor Posture → Country profiles → Theme cross-cuts → Lens panel
  → Decision Implications → Persona Implications → Historical Analogues → Watchlist
  → Geographic Reference appendix → Methodology + Limits → References → About.
- **8 v4 synthesis agents** with deep-analysis prompts (~30-45K tokens each):
  - Per top risk: 800-1200 word lead + causal chain (4-6 steps) + 3 second-order
    effects + historical analogue (episode/year/similarities/differences/lesson) +
    counter-narrative (150-200 word steelman) + quantified impact + watch signals +
    lens reading.
  - 5-7 tail risks: title + category + probability band + magnitude + 200-300w
    description + early-warning indicators + 30/90/180-day cascade + historical
    parallel + quantified impact.
  - 12-20 cross-impact couplings.
  - 4-6 historical analogue pairings.
  - 6-8 Bayesian prior→posterior updates.

### Architecture moves
- **Strategic Atlas relocated to back appendix** (was section 05 mid-brief in v3,
  now section 16 reference appendix in v4). The 12 maps remain available but no
  longer interrupt the per-risk argument flow.
- **Per-risk dedicated sections replace top-risks block**. Each of 10 risks gets
  its own 2-3 page block with embedded visuals + causal chain + analogue + counter +
  lens reading.
- **Tail Risks section is new** — Snow Leopards / Wild Cards / Black Swans before
  the central case, per Eurasia Red Herrings placement convention.
- **No full-page empty section dividers** — v3 had 8 wasted pages with just kicker +
  title; v4 uses inline `section_open()` (HR + kicker + title + summary).
- **Palette pulled in** — less salmon, deeper navy + deep red + restrained gold + pure
  white. Removed v3 vermillion entirely.
- **174mm safe-width** — all flowables clamped; tables auto-scale columns when total
  would exceed safe width.

### Output (in progress at time of writing)
- `output/pdfs_v4/` — 8 PDFs, ~150–250pp expected.
- v3 PDFs at `output/pdfs_v3/`, v2 at `output/pdfs_v2/`, v1 at `output/pdfs/` for comparison.
- `DESIGN_SYSTEM_V4.md` documents all v4 design choices, palette, layout principles.

---

entries.title: v3 data-driven editorial redesign
entries.body:
A second peer-benchmarked iteration on top of v2, focused on three explicit client demands:
(1) editorial-grade visual quality (FT / NYT / The Economist standard, not corporate teal);
(2) far heavier data density — maps for chokepoints, trade flows, energy, conflict, sanctions,
military posture, critical minerals, and trade corridors; (3) explicit *quantified business
impact* (Revenue-at-Risk, business-metric trigger thresholds, 30/60/90-day action plans) to
close the gap identified in the PwC C-suite outlook (April 2026): **65% of executives lack
the data to assess geopolitical risk; 68% can't translate uncertainty into business decisions**.

### New
- **Editorial palette** (`styles_v3.py`) — warm-cream paper background `#FAF6EE`, near-black ink
  `#0B1320`, Economist signal red `#C8102E`, FT editorial blue `#1F4986`, NYT vermillion `#D04A2E`,
  sophisticated mustard `#C8A845`. Times-Bold serif headers; Helvetica body; tabular numerals.
- **Static geopolitical reference data** (`gipre/data/geopolitical_static.py`) — chokepoints
  with daily oil throughput + trade $bn; 30 bilateral trade flows; critical-minerals concentration
  by mineral; semiconductor-leading-edge concentration by node; trade corridor waypoints (BRI,
  IMEC, INSTC, NSR, Middle Corridor, CPEC, Lobito); military bases; A2/AD missile ranges; OFAC
  SDN concentration; shadow-fleet flags; ACLED conflict hotspots; scenario-archetype impact templates.
- **Strategic Atlas** — 12 cartographic + chart exhibits per brief:
  1. Maritime chokepoint world map (marker area ∝ daily oil throughput)
  2. Chokepoint throughput bars with $bn annual trade
  3. Trade-flow arrow map (origin-destination, weight ∝ $bn, colour by type)
  4. Energy-flow world map (pipelines + LNG terminals; active/planned/destroyed)
  5. Conflict density / casualties world map (top-10 hotspots, marker ∝ 2025 fatalities)
  6. Conflict event-vs-fatality dual-axis bars
  7. OFAC SDN sanctions concentration choropleth (log scale)
  8. Military posture + A2/AD missile-range map
  9. Critical-minerals small-multiples (REE / Li / Co / Ni / graphite / U mining + refining shares)
  10. Critical-minerals stacked top-3 supplier bars
  11. Strategic trade corridors (BRI / IMEC / INSTC / NSR / Middle Corridor / CPEC / Lobito)
  12. Top bilateral trade flows Sankey-style
- **Quantified-impact components** in the PDF builder:
  - `quantified_impact_table()` — scenarios × {GDP %, Oil $/bbl, Equity %, FX-EM %, Trade %, Casualties k}
  - `business_trigger_table()` — scenario → business metric → numeric threshold → action
  - `action_plan_table()` — 30/60/90-day owner-tagged actions with KPI and revisit trigger
  - `revenue_at_risk_table()` — McKinsey value-at-stake decomposition (Revenue × Pr × Severity = EaR)
- **8 new synthesis agents** (`syntheses_v3/`) with quantified-impact prompts. Each returns:
  Chatham-tight executive summary, pull quote, 5-7 BLUF judgements with WEP + watch, 10 memetic
  top-risks with business triggers, quantified impact matrix (top-8 scenarios), 12 business
  triggers, 9-12 action items, 8-10 EaR rows, 5×5 strategic-options matrix, 9 persona implications.
- **New chart types** (`charts_v3.py`): quantified-impact heatmap with embedded values; forecast
  cone with explicit value labels at 6/12/24-month marks plus named scenario branches; Sankey
  flow; chokepoint throughput bars; critical-minerals stacked bars; conflict events vs fatalities
  dual-axis; WEP-banded scenario probability bars.
- **Editorial layout**: full-bleed cover banner, hero map, 5-cell stat strip with world-GDP
  reference, full-page section dividers, two-column country-card header, accent-bar callouts.
- **Documentation**: `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` (v2), three v3 research artefacts
  (`_research/v3_visualization_standards.md`, `v3_client_needs.md`, `v3_geopolitical_maps.md`).

### Output
- `output/pdfs_v3/` — 8 PDFs, **682 pages, ~81 MB total** (vs v2's 640pp/20MB; v1's 387pp/13MB).
- Master brief: **147pp**, 10.8 MB. Region briefs: 65–86pp, ~10 MB each.
- All maps render at 280 DPI on the warm-cream paper background.
- Every quantified figure cited in the agent JSONs (302 unique URL citations).

### Cost
- 8 v3 synthesis-agent runs at ~70-90K tokens each ≈ 600–700K tokens via Claude Pro/Max
  subscription. No external API.

### v3 architectural moves
- **Quantified impact replaces narrative-only** in every key surface. Per the PwC research,
  this is the documented #1 client gap (65% of execs lack data to assess geo risk).
- **Editorial palette replaces corporate teal**. Inspired by FT salmon-paper + Economist red
  + NYT vermillion + McKinsey deep navy. Times serif headers for editorial trust.
- **Strategic Atlas replaces a single choropleth map**. Eight maps with rich attributions and
  on-map labels supersede the v2 single risk choropleth.
- **30/60/90 action plans replace "decision implications"**. Each action carries an owner,
  KPI, and revisit trigger. Directly maps to McKinsey "where-to-play / how-to

entries.title: v2 brief redesign (peer-benchmarked)
entries.body:
The first build's PDFs were professional but template-driven. This release applies design
lessons from Eurasia Group, RANE, McKinsey, BCG, EY, RAND, Atlantic Council, CSIS, and
Chatham House to produce a 2-3× quality jump.

### New
- **v2 design system** (`gipre/reports/styles_v2.py`, `pdf_builder_v2.py`, `charts_v2.py`,
  `region_brief_v2.py`) — full peer-benchmarked rewrite of the rendering layer.
- **8 synthesis agents** dispatched (one per brief). Each reads its regional actor + theme +
  lens JSONs and produces a `GOVERNANCE_SYNTHESIS_OUTPUT_SCHEMA` payload with:
  - Chatham-style ≤400-word executive summary
  - Pull quote
  - 5-7 BLUF key judgements with WEP-compliant probabilities and observable thresholds
  - 10 memetic-titled top risks (Eurasia-style: "Maximum Donald", "Hormuz Hangover",
    "Frontier Fallout", "Powell's Ghost", "Silicon Tightrope", "Riyadh's Pakistan Hedge",
    "Strait Thunder Creep", "The Niger River Wall", "Africa Corps Long March", "USMCA's
    Last Summer", etc.)
  - Strategic options matrix (5 options × 5 scenarios)
  - 5-7 recommended actions with owner / horizon / revisit trigger
  - Persona implications for sovereign funds / central banks / defence ministries / energy corporates
- **Schema normalizer** (`region_brief_v2.normalize_synthesis`) handles the heterogeneous
  field-naming the synthesis agents produce.
- **v2 PDF brief layout**: cover → TOC → BLUF → executive summary + persona sidebars → top 10
  risks → master scenario library → actor posture → country deep-dives → theme cross-cuts →
  lens panel → decision implications → watchlist → methodology & limits → numbered references
  → About GIPRE.
- **New chart types**: BCG 2×2 scenario quadrant, EY geostrategic map scatter, Cone of
  Uncertainty fan, lens disagreement radar, theme severity risk clock, annotated probability
  bars with embedded values + CI error markers, diverging utility heatmap with embedded values.
- **New PDF components**: `CoverBanner`, `StatStrip`, `NumberedRiskBlock`, `CallOutBox`,
  `WEPChip`, `RiskChip` — all custom ReportLab flowables.
- **Words of Estimative Probability (WEP)** per ODNI IC Directive 203 surfaced as branded
  chips next to every probability.
- **Documentation**: new `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` records every peer pattern adopted, every pattern
  deliberately rejected, the full component inventory, typography hierarchy, palette,
  WEP ladder, and open design debts.
- **Honest self-critique**: `_research/v1_critique.md` documents every weak point in v1
  before redesign.
- **Peer research**: `_research/competitors_eurasia_rane.md`,
  `competitors_mckinsey_bcg_ey.md`, `competitors_rand_atlantic_csis_chatham.md` — three
  deep-research reports synthesised into 45 concrete design directives.

### Output
- `output/pdfs_v2/` — 8 PDFs, **640 pages total, 20.2 MB** (up from v1's 387pp / 12.8 MB).
- Master brief: **142pp** (vs. 105pp in v1).
- Region briefs: **63-78pp** each (vs. 33-47pp in v1).
- The v1 PDFs remain at `output/pdfs/` for side-by-side comparison.

### Cost
- 8 synthesis-agent runs at ~80-140K tokens each ≈ 800K-1.1M tokens, consumed via the
  Claude Pro/Max subscription. No external API.

### Known v2 design debts (deferred to v3)
- Page header section name is static (kicker) due to ReportLab onLaterPages single-pass
  binding. A PageTemplates-based v3 pass can resolve this.
- TOC uses approximate page numbers. ReportLab `TableOfContents` flowable is the v3 fix.
- Inline footnote markers in body text not yet wired; references remain an appendix list.
- Glossary, two-column body layout, and body-section pull-quotes deferred to v3.

entries.title: First 50-agent slice
entries.body:
**The MVP slice the Doc 6 Gap Audit recommends.**

### Built
- 65-layer architectural spine (`config/layers.yaml`) with 24 layers active and 41 stubbed-but-registered for systematic activation later.
- 50-agent registry (`config/agents.yaml`): 30 actor + 10 theme + 5 lens + 5 governance roles per Doc 6 §3.1 five-role taxonomy.
- 30 country / bloc actor profiles (`config/countries.yaml`).
- 10 priority themes (`config/themes.yaml`) with 70 stubbed for later activation.
- 20 lens panel (`config/lenses.yaml`): 16 canonical Western IR/PE lenses + 4 heterodox lenses (Tianxia, Eurasianism, Pan-African, Neo-Ottoman) per Doc 6 Gap 6.
- Master Scenario Library (`gipre/scenarios/library.py`): 100 scenarios anchored on the verbatim Doc 1 §3 L27 sample top-10 (Q4-2025 snapshot), extended combinatorially across 5 stress × 8 GP archetypes × 12 regional flashpoints.
- Engine modules: `core/audit`, `core/calibration`, `core/conformal`, `core/citations`, `core/registry`, `data/sources`, `data/fetch`, `scenarios/library`, `scenarios/qre`, `scenarios/probability`, `scenarios/triggers`, `synthesis/bps`, `synthesis/cascade`, `orchestration/contracts`, `orchestration/prompts`, `orchestration/runner`, `reports/styles`, `reports/charts`, `reports/maps`, `reports/pdf_builder`, `reports/compose`, `reports/region_brief`.
- 50 agent system-prompt markdowns (`agents/`), generated from YAML registries + persona briefings via `scripts/generate_agent_specs.py`.
- 8 PDF briefs (`output/pdfs/`): Master + 7 regional (North America, Europe, Greater Middle East, Asia-Pacific, South Asia, Africa, Latin America) — 387 pages total.

### Run
- 45 agents (30 actor + 10 theme + 5 lens) dispatched via Claude Code's Agent tool, no Anthropic API key required. Each agent did 8-15 web searches (WebSearch / WebFetch) against 2024-2026 OSINT, produced strict JSON conforming to its role's schema, with every numeric claim cited URL + retrieval-date.
- 302 unique URL citations across all agents.
- All agent outputs persisted as JSON in `runs/agents-2026-05-10/results/`.
- SHA-256 manifest hash chain in `runs/agents-2026-05-10/audit_ledger.jsonl` per Doc 1 §2.24 L24.

### Architectural decisions
- **Cicero / DiL-piKL replaced by LLM agents** per Doc 6 Gap 2. The 30 actor agents implement the L15 strategic-deep tier via Claude reasoning rather than the 1900-1914 Diplomacy-trained Cicero infrastructure that the original Doc 1 §2.11 specified.
- **WeasyPrint → ReportLab** for PDF rendering. WeasyPrint requires GTK-3 / Pango / Cairo, which has Windows compatibility issues. ReportLab is pure-Python, works everywhere. The brand palette and typography defaults from Doc 2 §10 are preserved in `gipre/reports/styles.py`.
- **All-Claude routing in this build.** The agent specs declare `backbone: claude-sonnet-4-6` (default) / `claude-opus-4-7` (critical) / `claude-haiku-4-5` (routine) tiers. Multi-vendor routing (DeepSeek for Tianxia, Qwen for Eurasianism, regional fine-tunes for Pan-African) is structurally accommodated but not yet wired. The lens specs explicitly note this gap.

### Documentation
- `README.md` — top-level overview + reproduction recipe
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — engine map, contracts, data flow, audit
- `EXPANSION_GUIDE.md` — Stage 0 → Stage 5 (full v9.0 enterprise) roadmap
- `AGENT_COVERAGE.md` — layer-by-layer + agent-by-agent scoresheet
- `CHANGELOG.md` — this file

### Honest limits (per Doc 6 §7)
1. Lens-pluralism is partially aspirational while all agents run on Claude.
2. Forecast accuracy < superforecasters; commercial wedge is scenario coverage + transparency, not point accuracy.
3. No back-tested track record yet — first quarterly falsification cycle starts from this build.
4. Single-tenant (founder profile only); customisation tiers L33-L40 stubbed.
5. Some agent JSONs returned non-strict schema fields (e.g., L17 returned prose for `weights_recommendation`); the synthesis composer is defensive against this.

### Cost
- Approximate Claude tokens consumed in dispatch of 45 agents × ~70K tokens each ≈ 3.15M tokens, all consumed via the user's $280 Claude Pro/Max subscription. No external API key was used.

---

## Pre-9.0 history

Owned by the source documents (`_source_docs/doc1_methodology_v9.md` Appendix C and Section S/T):

- v1.0 (2024-Q3): 16 layers, no scenario engine.
- v2.0 (2024-Q4): 24-layer H-MoE-BLF.
- v3.0–v5.0 (2025-Q1): refinements; lens panel finalised at 16.
- v6.0–v7.0 (2025-Q2): output and implementation companion docs v1.0.
- v8.0 (2025-Q4): Global Scenario Engine (L25–L29), Cascade Chain (L30–L32), Customisation Matrix (L33–L36) — 36 layers.
- v8.1 (2026-Q2): adds L37–L40 (four customisation tiers) and four time horizons; 40 layers.
- **v9.0 (2027 planned, current spec)**: adds L41–L65 (polycrisis, behavioural+LLM, adjacent fields); 65 layers — this is the document family extracted into `_source_docs/`.
- v10.0+ (2028+): causal-foundation models, multi-agent foundation models, quantum optimisation.
